Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (SLOs, fallback models, incident history)

Hi Alice / Samir 1

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Pain points you shared
- Recent production incidents (two in last 6 months) where inference endpoints degraded and regional failover didn't trigger cleanly.
- Visibility gaps: team lacks token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-route error tracing.
- Desire to avoid full outage by routing to cheaper fallback models/regions while keeping response quality acceptable.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Hosting fine-tuned open models on AWS (us-west-2); inference on mixed GPU fleet (some g4dn, some shared TPU-like instances via partner).
- Internal caching layer with short TTLs; prefix KV caching not in use for all routes.

Success criteria you mentioned
- 99.95% availability for critical routes (sub-100ms additional tail latency goal on failover).
- Predictable unit economics: cap monthly inference cost variance to +/-10%.
- Clear audit logs and proof points for upcoming procurement/infosec review.

Potential Redwood approaches we discussed
- Dedicated capacity for critical routes to guarantee throughput + predictable latency.
- Smart routing + model hierarchy: canonical model -> lighter quantized variant -> fallback tiny model in other region.
- Automatic prefix/KV caching to reduce cost and blast radius during load spikes.
- Observability: per-route token/latency/cost breakdowns and tracing to pinpoint regressions.

Requested deliverables / next steps (owners & timing)
1) Ben: send an SLA / SLO matrix + short design sketch for graceful degradation (attached). — Today (attached: 2026-02-20-ben-recap-sla-matrix.pdf)
2) Acme: share recent incident post-mortem(s) and preferred SLO targets. — Alice/Samir by EOW 2/27
3) Technical deep-dive (infra + security) with your engineering team — propose Wed 3/3 or Thu 3/4. Ben/Marissa to coordinate.
4) Security one-pager and SOC2 evidence pointers from Redwood — Marissa to attach. — Marissa to send by Mon 2/23 (attached: redwood-security-one-pager.pdf)

If that matches your notes, we'll lock the deep-dive time and circle back with a one-page plan that maps to your SLO targets and cost controls.

Ben

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns closely with our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Incident history: we had an autoscaling bug in Sept 2025 that caused ~45 mins of degraded responses for our Recommendations route (error rate spike + 3x latency tail). In Jan 2026, a config drift took down a model replica in us-west-2, and our cross-region failover had a 7 minute delay due to DNS TTLs and health-check timing.
- Current SLO targets: team is aiming for 99.95 for critical routes and 99.0 for non-critical. We understand tradeoffs of routing to smaller models but want to keep quality degradation within acceptable bounds for customer-facing flows.
- Stack details: model hosting is on EKS w/ custom autoscaler, inference on mixed GPU fleet; we also use a small Redis cluster for request caching.

We'll get the incident post-mortems to you by Monday and confirm availability for the 3/3 or 3/4 deep-dive. Either day should work for engineering — leaning to 3/3.

Thanks — appreciate the follow-up.
